A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-VAds benchmark and E-VAds-R1 model. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching experimental settings moved from the appendix into the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-density measurements, model and human benchmark results, training and input ablations, and a qualitative case study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds ASR-only evaluation results for four models in Table 4.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction pipeline, two-stage SFT/RL procedure, evidence-based rewards, and MG-GRPO formulation are retained. Renaming R2 to R3 preserves the scoring function and does not change the method.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, and five QA tasks remain unchanged. Table 4 adds a transcript-only scenario with visual input withheld, extending the previously evaluated Video and Video+ASR input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same model and human comparators. Table 4 retains Qwen3-Omni-Thinking, Keye1.5-VL, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, and E-VAds-R1; its added rows evaluate these existing models under another input condition.

E3.justification: The modality ablation gains an ASR-only control alongside video-only and combined inputs. Existing splits, training budgets, frame sampling, and judging procedures are unchanged; the settings in v3 Section 6.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix G. R2-to-R3 renaming leaves metric values unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Section 6.3 tests the benefit of adding ASR to video. v3 Section 6.4 additionally tests performance without visual input, providing complementary evidence about dependence on vision. Table 3's training/reward ablations and the appendix case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run uncertainty, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The human baseline's averaging over two independent annotators is retained from v1 Appendix G in v3 Section 6.1.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds ASR-only scores for four models, including S/R3/R5 scores of 0.162/0.404/0.597 for E-VAds-R1. Its existing video-only scores of 0.257/0.532/0.701 and combined-input scores of 0.320/0.577/0.736 remain unchanged. Other numerical tables and appendix findings are retained.

T1.justification: The density definitions, sampling equation, reward mapping, and group-normalized advantage remain mathematically unchanged. Relaxed-2/R2 becomes Relaxed-3/R3 with the same piecewise definition; no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the benchmark novelty claim, multimodal-density contribution, MG-GRPO contribution, and headline 109.2% relative improvement. The expanded conclusion restates these existing claims without changing their substantive scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ASR-only results as evidence that visual information is indispensable. Its Impact Statement also newly acknowledges persistent commercial, cultural/regional, creator-style, and platform-selection biases in source videos despite annotation safeguards.

D1.justification: v3's abstract newly provides a GitHub data-access URL. Hardware, training hyperparameters, annotation details, and prompts are retained, including settings relocated from Appendix G. The PDFs establish the new access disclosure but cannot verify the linked resource's contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Feng et al. (2026a,b) on text–3D retrieval and cross-scene alignment, citing them in Sections 2.2 and 4.2. The broader positioning against general VideoQA and advertising benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Experimental settings move from Appendix G to Section 6.1, subsequent subsections are renumbered, and the case study becomes Appendix G. v3 expands the conclusion, revises the modality-ablation discussion, harmonizes R3 terminology, and updates author and publication information; most prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains ASR-only rows, relabels Base/Base+ASR as Video/Video+ASR, and moves from page 8 to page 9. Table 3's caption adopts R3, and table widths, caption spacing, and surrounding layout change modestly. All figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's video-versus-video+ASR comparison, v3's ASR-only control provides useful evidence about dependence on visual content. Specific source-bias limitations improve transparency, while the data-access pointer and consistent R3 terminology improve usability. These are limited gains around an unchanged core method and headline evaluation.
